name: stuck-cursor
description:
A landscape that answers a next link with a page carrying that same next link -- the scroll is not advancing. Following it again can only produce the same page a third time, so the walk has to notice the repeat and stop; without that it spends the whole page ceiling re-fetching one page and then reports a truncation that is really a stuck cursor.

request_count is exact at 3: the token, page one, and the one re-fetch of the repeated link that reveals the repeat. A walk that does not notice issues more; one that stops too early issues fewer.

The third scripted response ends the scroll and is never reached while the check holds. It exists ONLY as a terminator, so a regression fails on the request count in one extra request rather than by looping to the page ceiling and timing out.

The repeated page carries a record with neither DiscoveryId nor DeviceID so the ids stay unique -- the point here is the request sequence, not the second page's contents.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in paged: the id is the bare Ivanti DiscoveryId with no tenant scope.

log_contains: ivanti-neurons: the scroll returned a next link it had already served
